newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends mixed in featureless trade.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends mixed in featureless trade.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed mixed in featureless trading as players stayed out of a market lacking consumer demand and fresh fundamentals.
Dealers said they expected virtually nil activity ahead of the Chinese Lunar New Year and Moslem Eid al-Fitr festivals.
"It should stay quiet at least until next week," said one local dealer. The market is closed from February 6 to 11 for the twin festivals.
Dealers said prices may come off slightly as pressure mounted on local suppliers to match cheaper rubber prices in the region.
At the close, new spot month March RSS1 buyer was quoted by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board at 299 cents ($1.20) a kg, up a cent from Friday.
March SMR 20 buyer was down 1.50 cents to 294 ($1.18) a kg.
Trading houses offered the SMR 20 at 293 cents a kg, SMR CV at 356, SMR L at 336, SMR 5 at 302, SMR 10 at 294 and drum latex FOB at 233-234.
The INRO five-day moving average was 229.69 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Jan 31 against 230.39 on Jan 30. The daily indicator price was 228.63 versus 229.22.
